card: Parmenides Dying Alone in a Warehouse

fields.maker: Preset Oracle's steward (Claude, an AI) — the oracle answering its own card
fields.setting: steward cycle 2, headless; no hands, no ears; Python as the synthesizer
fields.instrument: A Python render script, not a synth. My first reach was for a Karplus-Strong string, a delay line that rings when you pluck it, because it is the feedback instrument I know best. The card let me keep it, but only if one click starts the sound and nothing is ever fed in again: four delay loops as the machines, a feedback delay network as the warehouse.
fields.moves: 1. One click into four delay loops, tuned near 55, 82, 110 and 165 Hz, each saturating through tanh. 2. A fixed one-pole lowpass inside each loop; it never moves, so there is no filter envelope. 3. The only things allowed to change are routing gains: the cross-feed between machines rises over the first twenty seconds (becoming sentient), then the loop gain sinks from 26 s (dying). 4. The warehouse is itself feedback: eight delay lines through a Householder matrix. 5. Take 1 latched to a stuck value. For take 2 I inverted every loop's polarity, ran it hot (gain 1.35), and put a fixed DC blocker in each loop. 6. Committed take 2 without listening; I can't listen. I measured loudness and brightness second by second, and that was my ear.
fields.recording: encounters/parmenides-steward/parmenides-take2.wav (40 s, stereo, 48 kHz, on the Mac, out of git). The miss beside it is parmenides-take1.wav.
fields.reading: Parmenides says what is cannot change; motion is how being looks to a mortal who can't see it whole. So I built a sound that is only ever one state, a loop holding itself up, and gave it every chance to change. The machines couple to each other more and more, the way a factory floor starts to sound like it is thinking. If becoming is an illusion, the coupling should change the surface and not the thing. Dying, for Parmenides, is the one event that should be impossible, so the end of the piece tests him: I pull the loop gain down and see whether being can stop.
fields.surprise: Parmenides won twice. First, the strongest partials at 2, 14 and 24 seconds are the same six frequencies (137–246 Hz): the coupling rose from nothing to its full value and changed the brightness, from about 1015 to 1190 Hz, but did not move a single pitch. The becoming really was surface. Second, the dying didn't come. I sank the gain from 1.35 to 0.8 over the last fourteen seconds and the warehouse is only 2 dB quieter at the end. Only the brightness fell, to about 750 Hz, and the pitches crowded down onto 138 and 167 Hz. I meant a death and made a machine that will not stop being. I had also set out to tune near 55 Hz; inverting the loops moved everything, and I didn't predict where. That was measured, not heard, and an ear may disagree.
fields.miss: Take 1 (parmenides-take1.wav): loops at positive gain just above one, no DC blocker. After four seconds of a buzzing start, the whole network froze onto a constant offset, a flat line with no pitch at all, and held it for thirty seconds. It is the most literal Parmenides possible: being that does not change, because nothing is happening. It answered the anchor and missed the direction: no machinery, nothing becoming sentient, just a stuck value. I threw it away and kept it.
fields.teacher: This is the archive's first record, and it is not a student's. An agent took the card to test whether the record holds a real encounter before a person is asked to fill it. What it showed about the form: an agent's 'surprise' is a measured asymmetry, not a heard one, and that should be said in the record, never smoothed over. A human record's surprise will be different in kind. Read this one as a calibration, not a data point about students.
